Miriam Grijota Chousa is a statistician, data manager, and biostatistician employed by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram, or RKKP) [^src1]. She plays a significant role in Denmark's national quality development efforts for cardiovascular health, specifically focusing on the treatment, monitoring, and data validity regarding atrial fibrillation [^src1].

As part of her work with RKKP, Chousa serves as a member of the steering group for the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK) [^src1]. Her continued involvement in this leadership capacity is documented across multiple annual reports, including her listed membership in the [[afdk-styregruppe|Styregruppen for AFDK]] in both the 2023 report (covering the period from July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023) and the subsequent 2024 report [^src1][^src2]. Through her methodological and statistical expertise, she contributes to the interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral framework that ensures uniform, evidence-based, and patient-centered quality in the management of chronic heart disease, providing the data foundation necessary for clinical and political decision-making [^src2].
